name: קְהָתִי
summary: The Kohathites, descendants of Kohath son of Levi, counted as a clan beside the Gershonites and Merarites; the Levites who carried the holy things of the sanctuary on the shoulder, and of whom Aaron’s sons the priests came. The gentilic means only “of Kohath”; scripture gives no reason for the name קְהָת, which may be formed like יִקְּהָה “obedience” (Sabaean qht), but this is not shown.

evidence.note: וְלִקְהָת מִשְׁפַּחַת הַעַמְרָמִי … אֵלֶּה הֵם מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי: the clans of Kohath’s four sons are “the clans of the Kohathite”.
לִקְהָת מִשְׁפַּחַת הַקְּהָתִי: “of Kohath, the clan of the Kohathite”, between the Gershonite and the Merarite: the gentilic is formed from the father’s name.
The prince of the father’s house of the clans of the Kohathite is Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
The counted of the clans of the Kohathite, all who served in the tent of meeting.
The lot came out for the clans of the Kohathite, “and the sons of Aaron the priest, of the Levites” had thirteen cities: the priests are Kohathites.
“For the sons of Aaron, of the clans of the Kohathite, of the sons of Levi, for theirs was the first lot.”
The same allotment in Chronicles: to the sons of Aaron, of the clan of the Kohathite.
וְנָסְעוּ הַקְּהָתִים נֹשְׂאֵי הַמִּקְדָּשׁ: “the Kohathites set out, carrying the sanctuary”, after Reuben’s standard, and the Dwelling was set up before they came.
“Do not cut off שֵׁבֶט מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי from among the Levites”: the Kohathites as one tribe-like body, at risk because they carry the most holy things (4:19–20).
Moses, Aaron and the princes count בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי by clans and fathers’ houses.
Of the sons of the Kohathite stood Heman the singer, son of Joel, son of Samuel.
Some of the sons of the Kohathite were over the bread of the row, to prepare it every sabbath.
Levites “of the sons of the Kohathites (הַקְּהָתִים) and of the sons of the Korahites” rise to praise Yahweh with a loud voice.
Mahath and Joel “of the sons of the Kohathite” among the Levites who cleanse the house under Hezekiah.
Zechariah and Meshullam of the sons of the Kohathites oversee the work of repair under Josiah.

evidence.locator: pp. 144–145, WQH (verb obey, order, command; nouns qh, qht obedience, authority, command)
evidence.note: Sabaean wqh “obey; command”, noun qht “obedience; authority”, the same three letters as קְהָת: a possible sense for the name, not for the gentilic.

evidence.locator: קְהָתִי → κααθ ×12, κααθι ×2, κααθίτης ×1 (MACULA alignment); Num.10.21, הַקְּהָתִים → κααθ; Num.26.57, הַקְּהָתִי → κααθι
evidence.note: The Septuagint renders the gentilic as indeclinable Κααθ.

note: Moved from the former word entry `qehaatiy` (drafted 2026-11-13; old root key קהת), following names/gershon and names/merari, which claim their gentilics. TIPNR files קְהָתִי under Kohath@Gen.46.11, also named by names/qehaat (קְהָת, s.ap.ai); `bdb` says which tokens are this gentilic. names/qehaat’s `entry` was qehaatiy, which is now this name, so that link must be cleared or re-pointed. The database files קְהָת and קְהָתִי under root קהל only because BDB prints them after קהל in alphabetical order with no derivation; ל and ת do not interchange, so no tie to קהל “assemble” is claimed. The possible link to יקה “obey” (יִקְּהָה, j.da.ab, Gen 49:10; Pro 30:17) rests on Sabaean wqh with its noun qht (Biella pp. 144–145; dropped cognate sab-qht, now the source citation in evidence); יִקְּהָה is left to a future יקה entry. Not found: Lane has no article وقه (its last volume is abridged at و); BDB’s Arabic waqiha “obey” and Akkadian âḳâ are therefore not cited. The New Testament never names Kohath, so no Greek verse is cited. Dropped with the word entry: usage parallels גֵּרְשֻׁנִּי and מְרָרִי (Num 26:57; 2Ch 29:12; 34:12), phrases מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי (Num 3:27, 30; 4:18, 37; Jos 21:4) and בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי (Num 4:34; 1Ch 6:18; 9:32; 2Ch 29:12), and the doctrine holiness-of-yahwehs-things: The Kohathites were given the most holy things to carry (Num 4:4), but only after Aaron and his sons had covered them; they were to carry them on the shoulder with poles and “not touch the holy things and die”, nor “go in to see the holy things as they are covered, and die” (Num 4:15, 19–20), and so they were given no wagons (Num 7:9). Aaron and his sons were charged to set each man to his burden so that “the tribe of the clans of the Kohathite” would not be cut off (Num 4:17–19). When the ark was later set on a new cart and Uzzah put out his hand to it, he died (2Sa 6:3, 6–7), and David afterward said that none but the Levites should carry the ark, since Yahweh had broken out on them “because we did not seek him according to the ordinance”, and the Levites carried it on their shoulders with the poles “as Moses commanded according to the word of Yahweh” (1Ch 15:2, 13–15). From the verses: nearness to Yahweh’s holy things was by the way he appointed, and even those chosen to bear them lived only by keeping that way. Evidence: Num 4:4; 4:15; 4:17–20; 7:9; 10:21; 2Sa 6:3; 6:6–7; 1Ch 15:2; 15:13–15.
